title: Middag
about: One song in two arrangements, above ground (group 'open') and underground (group 'cave'). The game crossfades the two groups by the player's surroundings; the faders are the mix, not a suggestion. Every lane of a group takes that group's gain. Written levels are each arrangement ALONE at full fader; both at full (a plain player) is about 3 dB louder than intended.

roles.lead: a tune: the flute's calls, the tines' B tune and answers
roles.foundation: bass and the guitar's picking, the pulse
roles.bed: sustained strings or glass: the first to smear under a cave reverb
roles.sparkle: high, struck colour (kalimba): shares the top with the birdsong outdoors

crossfade.control: x, 0 = in the open … 1 = enclosed in rock: the same balance the game's 73×73 survey sets between the open and cave convolvers, smoothed (a time constant of about 3 s) so that a tunnel mouth does not flutter
crossfade.note: taudplay: setVoiceGain(lane, gain, fade_ms) on every lane of both groups whenever the smoothed x has moved by more than about 0.02. The two arrangements never clash, so any x is a valid mix, and x = 0.5 is the fullest form of the piece.
